{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-nj-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"b831ae8fc5ea516f4f4de93e530ced81b6442630d32186dba5700c2641f3aef7","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-nj-class-d:lineage:10","source_registry_sha256":"057b72c7c679c997f56ae00ef97a6b14dbe264551f4121b9bf67b0457d9cf7c1","source_liveness_sha256":"1ca7bfbb9e3c0a6b19e5e808ecab6fe8329f3b4799e394abc260d65c1d6513e7"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driver testing: ID, vision, knowledge test and road test","heading":"C — Driver testing: ID requirements, vision screening, the knowledge test, interpreters, transfers, the road test and vehicle rejection","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Driver testing: ID requirements, vision screening, the knowledge test, interpreters, transfers, the road test and vehicle rejection
Knowledge domain: what every applicant must bring and pass before a New Jersey license is issued — ID verification, the vision screening, the knowledge test and its language and interpreter options, transfer rules, the road test checklist and the vehicle problems that end a road test before it starts.

FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Every applicant for a New Jersey driver license must have all the documents needed to satisfy the 6-Point ID Verification. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
REAL ID license or non-driver ID applicants must satisfy the 2+1+6 model: two proofs of New Jersey address, one proof of Social Security number and documents meeting the six-point rule. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Every motorist must pass a vision screening; the MVC may send applicants with impaired vision to a physician and may periodically require a recheck. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
The knowledge test has 50 questions, plus a survey question about organ donation. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
The knowledge test is offered in English and American Sign Language, and also in Albanian, Arabic, Chinese, French, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Turkish. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
An applicant who cannot read in any language is given headphones and takes the knowledge test orally. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
If your native language is not offered you may use a state-approved interpreter, but only after first attempting the test in one of the offered languages. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
An applicant who needs an interpreter must tell the MVC at least two weeks before the planned date of the written knowledge test. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
The MVC provides approved interpreters for Deaf or Hard of Hearing applicants and pays the knowledge-test interpreter fees once a completed payment voucher form is submitted. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0032]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A02
An approved foreign-language interpreter is someone listed on the Registry of Interpreters and Agencies kept by the NJ Administrative Office of the Courts, Language Services Section. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A02
An approved deaf or hard of hearing interpreter either holds certification from the National Registry of Interpreters for the Deaf and is on file with the NJ Division of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing, or has been evaluated by that Division and placed on its approved list. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A02
Basic license applicants need 20/50 vision, with or without corrective lenses. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A02
An applicant who sees with only one eye must have that eye meet the 20/50 rule and bring documentation signed by a licensed physician. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A02
CDL applicants need 20/40 vision in both eyes, with or without corrective lenses, and must tell red, green and amber lights apart. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A02
To pass the written test, 80 percent of the answers must be correct, which is 40 of the 50 questions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
Applicants must tell the examiner about health problems, and a medical review may be necessary. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0033]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A03
Knowledge and road tests may be waived for transfer applicants aged 18 or older with a valid, non-provisional license from any of the 50 states, the District of Columbia, Samoa, Guam, Puerto Rico or the US Virgin Islands. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A03
Transfer applicants still submit the 6-Point ID documents, receive a four-year basic New Jersey license and must surrender the out-of-state license. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A03
An out-of-state applicant aged 17 to 18 with a valid license receives a probationary license for one year and must follow New Jersey's GDL rules. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A03
Every out-of-country applicant must pass the knowledge test and vision screening and may also have to pass a road test; the results are valid for two years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A03
Signed in August 2015 and in force from March 1, 2016, Nikhil's Law amended N.J.S.A. 39:3-41 to stress the dangers of ignoring New Jersey traffic laws. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A03
The Safety Pledge to Nikhil commits drivers to stop completely, stay alert, talk safe with a hands-free system and plan ahead by allowing an extra 5 minutes for every trip. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0034]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A04
Eligible voters can start voter registration at any MVC Licensing Center while applying for or renewing a license or non-driver ID, and the registration deadline is 21 days before an election. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A04
Address changes must be done online, and the MVC then asks whether the change should also update your voter record. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A04
The law requires you to give the MVC your current New Jersey home address, and a replacement license showing the new address can be ordered after the change is processed. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0035]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A05
Once the knowledge test, vision screening and any required behind-the-wheel course are passed, the MVC validates the permit for practice driving. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: A05
GDL permit holders under 21 need at least six months of supervised practice with at least 50 hours, 10 of them in darkness, before a road test appointment. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A05
A completed BA-CSD form from a parent, guardian or supervising driver must be presented at the time of the road test appointment. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F29 | anchor: A05
GDL permit holders aged 21 or older need at least three months of supervised practice before a road test appointment. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F30 | anchor: A05
Practice driving is not allowed on the road test course or in the parallel parking area. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F31 | anchor: A05
Road test applicants must bring original documents: 6 points of ID, a legible unlaminated validated permit, a valid inspection sticker or the official card saying none is required, and valid registration and insurance ID cards for the test vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F32 | anchor: A05
GDL applicants must also have 2 red GDL decals properly mounted on the test vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F33 | anchor: A05
The examiner must be able to reach the foot brake or a parking brake mounted to the right of the driver. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F34 | anchor: A05
Autocycles and self-parking vehicles cannot be used, and the signals, brake lights and windshield wipers must all work. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F35 | anchor: A05
A rental car is allowed only if the applicant is named as a driver on the rental agreement, and the applicant must arrive with a licensed driver. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec03-F36 | anchor: A06
A licensed driver must stay in the vehicle with the applicant at all times, and the car may not be moved even in the road test line without one. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F37 | anchor: A06
If the accompanying driver is licensed outside New Jersey or has under three years of experience, that person must drive the vehicle to the road test area. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F38 | anchor: A06
The MVC does not supply road test vehicles, and only MVC examiners may be in the vehicle during the test. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F39 | anchor: A06
If the test vehicle has a standard transmission, the examiner will ask the applicant to show correct gear shifting. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec03-F40 | anchor: A07
The basic road test covers driving in reverse, following other vehicles, nearing corners and intersections, parallel parking, sitting properly with a seat belt, starting, steering, stopping at signs, stopping smoothly, turning, turning around, using the horn and yielding right-of-way. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec03-F41 | anchor: A07
After passing the road test you receive an authorization for licensing, and the permit, the authorization and 6 Points of ID must be taken to a Licensing Center. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec03-F42 | anchor: A07
An applicant never before licensed anywhere receives a Class D basic or probationary license, and the MVC monitors that driver's habits for one year. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec03-F43 | anchor: A08
Common road test vehicle rejections include an improper, expired or missing inspection sticker, no examiner access to a brake, poor brakes, a lit brake warning light and unsafe tires. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0039]

Misconceptions: the road test grades the vehicle as well as the driver, so a defective car can end the test before it starts; an interpreter is not available until the applicant first tries the test in an offered language; the accompanying driver, not the applicant, may have to drive to the test site; the organ donation survey question comes in addition to the fifty test questions.
Mnemonics: pass the written test with forty of fifty, eighty percent; see at twenty-fifty for a basic license; the Nikhil pledge is Stop, Stay alert, Talk safe, Plan ahead.
Glossary: Six-Point ID Verification means the point-based identity document rule; authorization for licensing means the examiner's pass slip taken to a Licensing Center; BA-CSD form means the certification of supervised driving from a parent, guardian or supervising driver; accompanying driver means the licensed driver who brings the applicant to the road test.
Dynamic facts: the language list, interpreter registries, election deadlines, websites and phone numbers can change; confirm them on the MVC and Division of Elections websites.
